chapter: Family and the lake excursion boats
title: Excursion boat route and trips with bands
summary: The boats docked at Spanish Fort and West End, reached by streetcar. They left early with a band playing and dancing, and Ernie has a photo of the Camellia sinking.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: On this side, did they tie up, did you say they tied up at Milburn? Or at Spanish Fort?
At Spanish Fort, right there by the New Orleans Country Club.

My mom had a Southern Yacht Club. Like Southern Yacht Club. That's right, West End. Right, West End. Southern Yacht Club. You catch the West End called Canal Street. They used to have one car and they had about four or five other cars attached to it. They were dead, they had no motors to them. Just the one, yeah, just like a train. But matter of fact, in front of them, how many people going across the lake and they would hitch on more? Sometimes it'd be eight or nine cars and be on Canal Street. All these together, going to West End.
They wouldn't put on the other cars, just hook on, you know, something like that. That's right.
And take you to West End. And you'd have to get out there for about six in the morning. That boat would pull out for about seven thirty. Eight, nine o'clock, they'd be out on the lake.
How many trips a day did they make?
I made one trip. See, by the time they'd get to Mounderville, it'd be about near 11 o'clock.

I mean, the band is playing. They got to stay there and let people off in Mounderville and people getting on to go to Madison and the band is playing, they're dancing on the boat and leave there then they'd go to Madison, see? And they'd tie up overnight. They'd probably leave that Monday evening or maybe that Tuesday. Sometimes they'd leave

on Tuesday. And then later on, they'd start making an excursion with the band on Wednesday, then on Sunday morning, Saturday, and they wouldn't come back until Sunday and sometimes they'd come back Saturday night and go Sunday morning and come back Sunday night. You know, I have business that's pretty good, you know. Yeah. That's right.
I have a picture of the camellia book. Have you ever seen it?
I've seen the picture of the postcards about that size and other little books on the way too.
I have a picture of it when it was sinking.
Oh, really? Let's see if I can find it. Yeah. Can you stop it? Yeah, sure. I'll run it for a minute to come find it. You remember the other community you do, Harold? You ever played?
